questions.question: When A level results first went out on 13 August, which grades were issued, and what rule was in effect by 26 August?
Could a pupil who had evidence of discriminatory grading bypass the school, and what would happen to the award if wrongdoing was proved?
How can the figures of about four in ten and more than two in three both describe upward revisions to A levels?
What provision was made for private candidates left without a summer result, and what later figure shows that people without a summer grade actually used it?
Who acknowledged that the initial results had caused young people distress, and could the later analysts identify which individuals suffered most?
Among pupils who lost a first-choice university place because of the initial A level result, how many regained that same place before its deadline after grades changed?
